children: The debate over artificial intelligence investing has shifted. The question is no longer whether demand exists, but whether enough capacity can be built, at acceptable returns, to meet it Wells Fargo's Investment Institute says.

Falling model costs and intensifying competition have fueled concern that economics will deteriorate. Wells Fargo’s Investment Institute takes the opposite view: cheaper inference is more likely to accelerate adoption than to shrink the market.

That next chapter is being written at inference, not training. Every user query and every agentic workflow—chains of model calls, validation steps and tool use—consumes compute. Rising usage can therefore offset lower unit prices and keep demand firm for processors, networking, cloud services, data centers and electricity.

Power availability is becoming one of the tightest constraints in the ecosystem, which in turn supports continued investment across the physical infrastructure stack. Infrastructure remains essential.

Yet the financial firm sees the next stage of value creation tilting toward software platforms that own proprietary data, control mission-critical workflows and operate as control towers for governance, security and model orchestration. Those platforms sit closer to the customer and the data; they may capture a growing share of the economics even as the hardware build-out continues.

title: Power constraints reinforce the case for AI infrastructure spending, Wells Fargo says
